long_biography.plain_text:
Arnold trained as a motor mechanic and began with a tyre and bodywork business in a farm workshop. A roadside encounter with a wheelchair user prompted him to redesign vehicles for independent access. He then created Space Drive, an electronic steering, braking and acceleration system that allowed drivers with severe physical disabilities to control a car without conventional pedals or a steering wheel.

Through Paravan, Arnold combined vehicle conversion, powered wheelchairs, driving instruction and electronic controls into an integrated mobility business. He later placed Space Drive in a Schaeffler joint venture to pursue industrial automotive applications, serving as chief executive before selling his remaining stake. After that exit, he returned his attention to wholly owned Paravan and the development of accessible mobility concepts.
